name: sort-heap
axis: sort — HAND-WRITTEN heapsort, the same algorithm in all four; branchy, cache-hostile random access over a large array
n: N=1000000 i32, ROUNDS=4 (4 sorts of fresh unsorted data, ~84M sift steps)
nPython: N=1000000 i32, ROUNDS=1 (4x fewer rounds; multiply Python's wall time by 4 to compare)
notes: NOT a library-sort comparison: nothing here calls Array.prototype.sort, Vec::sort_unstable or sorted(). Sift-down is a function in all four (called ~2N times per round, i.e. ~1/21 of the sift steps, so call overhead is not the axis). Data comes from a MINSTD LCG (seed*48271 % 2147483647); all intermediates stay under 2^47 so JS Numbers are exact. Output is three lines: a sampled checksum (every 4096th element, accumulated across rounds), the adjacent-inversion count (0 proves the sort is correct), and the last round's full sum. The stream continues across rounds, so each round sorts different data and the work is linear in ROUNDS. VL LIMITATION hit while authoring: the emitter rejects a bare `return` in a void function, so the early exit from sift-down is spelled as a `cont` flag in ALL FOUR languages to keep them equivalent. Scale-verified by doubling ROUNDS: vl 1.93x, rs 2.04x, js 2.01x, py 1.80x.
